quotes.text: Two ships of the Royal Norwegian Navy have borne the name HNoMS "Draug", after the sea revenant Draugr:

The draugr or draug (Old Norse: "draugr" , plural draugar ; modern Icelandic: "draugur" , Faroese: "dreygur" and Danish, Swedish, and Norwegian: "draug" ), also called aptrganga or aptrgangr , literally "again-walker" (Icelandic: "afturganga" ) is an undead creature from Norse mythology.

evidence.title: Wight
evidence.text: Wight is an English word, from Old English "wiht", and used to describe a creature or living sentient being.

evidence.title: Wight
evidence.text: It is akin to Old High German "wiht", meaning a creature or thing.

evidence.title: Wight
evidence.text: In its original usage the word "wight" described a living human being.

evidence.title: Wight
evidence.text: More recently, the word has been used within the fantasy genre of literature to describe undead: corpses with a part of their decayed soul still in residence, often draining life from their victims.

evidence.title: Wight
evidence.text: The earliest example of this usage in English is in William Morris's translation of the Grettis Saga, where draug is translated as "barrow wight".

evidence.title: Wight
evidence.text: Notable later examples include the undead Barrow-wights from the works of J. R. R. Tolkien, the reanimated creatures killed by the Others from the works of George R. R. Martin and in the HBO adaption of A Song of Ice and Fire, and the level-draining wights of "Dungeons & Dragons" role-playing game franchise.

evidence.title: HNoMS Vidar (N52)
evidence.text: HNoMS "Vidar" (N52) was a Royal Norwegian Navy minelayer and command vessel.

evidence.title: HNoMS Vidar (N52)
evidence.text: "Vidar" was built by Mjellem & Karlsen in Bergen in 1977, and named after Odin's son Vidar from Norse mythology.

evidence.title: HNoMS Vidar (N52)
evidence.text: The vessel was the command ship for NATO's "Mine Counter Measures Force North" (MCMFORNORTH) in 2004 and 2005.

evidence.title: HNoMS Vidar (N52)
evidence.text: In 2006 she was sold to Lithuania and given the name "Jotvingis".

evidence.title: HNoMS Vidar (N52)
evidence.text: The Lithuanian Navy uses her as a command and support ship.

evidence.title: HNoMS Nordkapp
evidence.text: HNoMS "Nordkapp" was the lead ship of the "Nordkapp" class of fishery protection vessels.

evidence.title: HNoMS Nordkapp
evidence.text: She was launched 18 August 1937 at Horten naval shipyard, with yard number 123.

evidence.title: HNoMS Nordkapp
evidence.text: She had one sister ship, HNoMS "Senja".

evidence.title: HNoMS Nordkapp
evidence.text: "Nordkapp" was named after the North Cape in Finnmark.

evidence.title: HNoMS Nordkapp
evidence.text: As was typical of her class, "Nordkapp" was very unstable in rough seas and was viewed from the beginning as a second-rate vessel.

evidence.title: HNoMS Nordkapp
evidence.text: "Nordkapp" sailed throughout the Second World War and saw service in several theatres.

evidence.title: HNoMS Troll (1910)
evidence.text: The destroyer HNoMS "Troll, known locally as "Torpedojager Troll (litt.: "torpedo hunter"), was the second destroyer built for the Royal Norwegian Navy, as the second ship of the "Draug"-class destroyers.

evidence.title: HNoMS Troll (1910)
evidence.text: She was built at the naval shipyard in Horten, with yard number 104.

evidence.title: HNoMS Troll (1910)
evidence.text: She was kept in service long after she was obsolete, and took part in the defence of Norway after the German invasion in 1940.

evidence.title: HNoMS Draug (1908)
evidence.text: HNoMS "Draug" was the lead ship of the three-ship "Draug" class of destroyers built for the Royal Norwegian Navy in the years 1908–1913.

evidence.title: HNoMS Draug (1908)
evidence.text: The four-stacked destroyer was kept in service long after she was obsolete, and took part in the defence of Norway during the German invasion in 1940.

evidence.title: HNoMS Garm (1913)
evidence.text: HNoMS "Garm" was the third destroyer built for the Royal Norwegian Navy, and was a "Draug" class destroyer.

evidence.title: HNoMS Garm (1913)
evidence.text: "Garm" was constructed several years after her two sister ships, but to the same plans.

evidence.title: HNoMS Garm (1913)
evidence.text: She was built at the naval shipyard in Horten, with yard number 107.
